satisfied_inclusion_points: Full research article in English with full text available.
Original primary research proposing an automated approach.
Uses NLP to extract/generate BPMN process models from natural-language text.
Provides a concrete method/pipeline and empirical evaluation on 47 text–model pairs.
evidence_highlights: “we tackle this problem based on an automatic approach to generate BPMN models from natural language text.”
“We combine existing tools from natural language processing in an innovative way and augmented them with a suitable anaphora resolution mechanism.”
“we develop an approach to directly extract business process models from textual descriptions.”
“The evaluation of our technique shows that for a set of 47 text-model pairs from industry and textbooks, we are able to generate on average 77% of the models correctly.”
“Section 3… discusses sentence level analysis… text level analysis… describes the generation of a BPMN model.”
decision_rationale: The paper is an English, full-text, primary research article presenting an NLP-based method (including anaphora resolution) to extract BPMN process models from natural-language text. It details a concrete pipeline and reports an empirical evaluation on 47 text–model pairs with quantitative results, satisfying all Stage 2 inclusion criteria and triggering no exclusions.

source_record_provenance.record_title: Automated generation of business process models from natural language input

satisfied_inclusion_points: Full research article in English with full text available (EDOC 2022 LNCS paper).
Primary research presenting an original NLP approach (GPT-3 with in-context learning) for process extraction.
Specifically targets extracting process entities and relations from natural-language process descriptions.
Describes a concrete method and reports experiments/empirical assessment (tasks T1–T3 with results).
evidence_highlights: Title: "Extracting Business Process Entities and Relations from Text Using Pre-trained Language Models and In-Context Learning"
Abstract: "investigate the usage of the native GPT-3 model... for the extraction of typical business process entities and relationships"
Sect. 3.1: defines questions Q1–Q3 to extract activities, participants, performs relation, and directly-follow relation.
Sect. 4 (Empirical Assessment): "We perform all the experiments adopting the text-davinci-001 engine..." and evaluates tasks T1–T3.
Results discussion: "the results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach... while highlighting the challenge posed by control flow relations."
decision_rationale: The paper is an English full research article presenting an original NLP method for extracting business process entities and relations from natural-language text using GPT-3 and in-context learning, and includes a concrete pipeline with an empirical assessment (tasks T1–T3 and reported results). No exclusion criteria are triggered.
